Information in the December 13, 2017 FOMC statement conveys a constructive macro backdrop—“solid” growth and a “strong” labor market—paired with below-target inflation and a 25 bp rate hike to 1.25–1.50%. The Committee’s emphasis on “gradual” increases is consistent with estimated, inertial Taylor-type rules and forward-looking policy behavior documented by Clarida, Galí, and Gertler, and with flexible inflation-targeting frameworks (Svensson and Woodford) that weigh real activity against a symmetric 2% inflation objective. Implementation via interest on reserves and ON RRP rates aligns with modern operating frameworks discussed by Goodfriend (2002), while continued balance-sheet normalization signals a predictable path consistent with the literature’s preference for transparency and rule-like behavior. Two dovish dissents reflect concern over persistent sub-2% inflation, but with expectations anchored and policy still accommodative (rate “below longer-run” levels), the overall tone skews modestly positive for the outlook, albeit cautiously hawkish for financial conditions.
